front.title: The Item and Collection Link Relations

abstract.t: RFC 5988 standardized a means of indicating the relationships between resources on the Web. This specification defines a pair of reciprocal link relation types that may be used to express the relationship between a collection and its members.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: RFC 5988 standardized a means of indicating the relationships between resources on the Web. This specification defines a pair of reciprocal link relation types that may be used to express the relationship between a collection and its members.
These link relation types can be applied to a wide range of use cases across multiple media types. For example, the 'collection' and 'item' link relation types are used in these media types:

section.name: Link Relations
section.t: The following link relations are defined.

section.name: 'item'
section.t: When included in a resource that represents a collection, the 'item' link relation identifies a target resource that represents a member of that collection.
For example, if a resource represents a catalog of products, that same representation may include one or more links to resources that represent members of that catalog.
section.artwork:
...

Product Group X Listing

... View Product X001 View Product X002 ...
section.t: or, in the case of a Link Header field
section.artwork: Link: <...>; rel="item"; title="View Product X001" Link: <...>; rel="item"; title="View Product X002"

section.name: 'collection'
section.t: When included in a resource that represents a member of a collection, the 'collection' link relation identifies a target resource that represents a collection of which the context resource is a member.
For example, if a resource represents a single product in a catalog, that same representation may include a link to a resource that represents a product group to which this single product belongs:
section.artwork: Return to Product Group X
section.t: or, in the case of a Link Header field
section.artwork: Link: <...>; rel="collection"; title="Return to Product Group X"
section.t: Since it is possible that a resource could be a member of multiple collections, multiple 'collection' link relations may appear within the same representation:
section.artwork: View other widgets View all discontinued items
section.t: The target resource representation need not be restricted to representing a list. It may simply be a document that provides details on the collection of which the context resource is a member:
section.artwork: Link: <...>; rel="collection"; title="Shakespeare's Collected Works - A History"
section.t: It should also be noted that the same link might represent an 'item' in one collection as well as a 'collection' itself. In this case, both link relation values can be applied to the same link:
section.artwork: Link: <...>; rel="collection item"; title="A Review of Issac Asimov's Collected Works - Vol. I"

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA has registered the 'collection' and 'item' link relations below as per .

dl.dd: The target IRI points to a resource that is a member of the collection represented by the context IRI.
The target IRI points to a resource that represents the collection resource for the context IRI.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The two link relation types defined in this document do not introduce any new security issues to those which are discussed in Section 7 of RFC5988 .

section.name: Internationalisation Considerations
section.t: The 'item' and 'collection' link relation types do not have any internationalization considerations other than those which are discussed in Section 8 of RFC5988 .
